claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

is_adopting.description: Whether the claimant is adopting the child.

child_has_moved_in.description: Whether the child being adopted has come to live with the claimant.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm asking about my daughter Alex. She's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation and Alex's circumstances.

**Do you currently live in the UK, and does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. But no, Alex doesn't live with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex doesn't live with you currently, I need to understand more about the situation.

**Can you tell me who Alex is living with, and do you make any financial contributions towards her upkeep (such as for clothes, food, pocket money, or accommodation)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with her other parent right now. I do contribute financially though - I help out with things like clothes, school supplies, and other expenses for her.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility properly, I need to understand more about the financial contributions you're making.

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep each week or month, and is the other parent currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £30 a week towards Alex's upkeep. As far as I know, her other parent isn't claiming Child Benefit for her.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**Are you contributing this £30 per week regularly, and has this arrangement been in place for more than 8 weeks? Also, when did Alex go to live with her other parent?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I've been contributing the £30 a week regularly. It's been going on for quite a while now - definitely more than 8 weeks. Alex has been living with her other parent for some time now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I need to clarify one more important point to make a proper assessment.

**Just to confirm - has anyone else (including Alex's other parent) actually claimed Child Benefit for Alex, or is nobody currently receiving Child Benefit for her?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody is currently receiving Child Benefit for her. Her other parent hasn't claimed it.

## Eligibility Assessment Result

**Good news!** Based on the information you've provided, **you are ELIGIBLE to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

### Here's why:

Even though Alex (age 8) doesn't live with you, you qualify for Child Benefit because:

1. **Alex is under 16** - She meets the age requirement for Child Benefit
2. **You live in the UK** - You meet the residency requirement
3. **You're making sufficient contributions** - Your regular £30 per week contribution towards Alex's upkeep (for clothes, school supplies, and other expenses) meets or exceeds the Child Benefit payment amount
4. **Regular contributions over time** - You've been making these contributions consistently for more than 8 weeks
5. **No one else is claiming** - Alex's other parent is not currently receiving Child Benefit for her

Under the rules, while Child Benefit typically only continues for 8 weeks after a child goes to live with someone else, it can continue for longer if you contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment towards your child's upkeep. Since you're contributing £30 per week regularly, you meet this requirement.

### Next Steps:
You should make a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. Only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child, so it's important that you claim it if the other parent isn't doing so.
